insights.headline: Gold, silver slip as oil rebound keeps December Fed hike bets near 90%
insights.summary: Gold and silver eased on Wednesday, October 21, as Brent crude's rebound toward $112 revived inflation concerns and kept December Fed rate-hike expectations near 90%. MCX December gold fell Rs 389 to Rs 1,46,130 per 10 grams and December silver dropped Rs 1,733 to Rs 2,09,752 per kg; Comex gold traded near $4,139 an ounce with silver near $57.57. Analysts are split: a confirmed move above $4,217 could reopen a path toward $4,820, but a break below $4,070 risks gold toward $4,000 and silver toward $50.
points: MCX December gold down Rs 389 at Rs 1,46,130 per 10g; silver down Rs 1,733 at Rs 2,09,752 per kg.
Comex gold near $4,139 an ounce, silver near $57.57 as Brent crude rebounded toward $112.
December Fed rate-hike odds near 90% versus 16% for the October 27-28 meeting.
$4,217 is the breakout trigger toward $4,820; below $4,070, gold could test $4,000 and silver $50.
NDB Wealth sees $4,200-5,000 gold over 12-24 months on central-bank and Asian demand.

trending.title: Oil revives the Fed-hike threat for bullion
trending.summary: Brent’s rebound toward $112 and tanker attacks in West Asia have revived inflation fears; December Fed hike bets sit near 90%, pressuring gold and silver on MCX and Comex.

trending.title: Gold’s technical tug-of-war
trending.summary: One camp sees a confirmed break above $4,217 reopening $4,820; the other warns a slip below $4,070 targets $4,000 — with silver’s $55 line the equivalent tripwire.

trending.title: Central banks still set the long game
trending.summary: The NDB Wealth report sees $4,200-5,000 gold over 12-24 months on central-bank and Asian demand — even as Russia sold 62 tonnes of reserves, its biggest drawdown since 1998.

items.title: Gold, silver fall as higher crude oil prices revive rate-hike concerns
items.summary: Gold and silver futures slipped in Wednesday's morning session as elevated crude prices revived inflation worries and further US rate-hike fears. MCX December gold fell Rs 389 to Rs 1,46,130 per 10 grams and December silver dropped Rs 1,733 to Rs 2,09,752 per kg; Comex gold traded near $4,139 an ounce and silver near $57.57, with West Asia tensions keeping supply fears in focus.

items.title: Gold (XAU/USD) Price Forecast: $4,217 Breakout Puts Bulls Back in Control
items.summary: FXEmpire’s technical analysis puts gold at a pivotal juncture, with support near $4,066 and resistance at $4,217. A confirmed move above $4,217 on daily and weekly charts would signal a bullish reversal and could open a path toward $4,820; failure at resistance risks a deeper leg of the correction.

items.title: Gold and Silver Price Forecast: Breakdown Risk Persists as Oil Rebounds
items.summary: Gold consolidated around $4,120 on Wednesday, held below $4,200 as December Fed rate-hike expectations sat near 90% and Brent crude rebounded toward $112. FXEmpire warns a break below $4,070 could drag gold toward $4,000, while silver risks a drop toward $50 if $55 support fails.

items.title: Gold may trade up to USD 5,000/oz over next two years as central banks sustain demand: Report
items.summary: Gold could hold $4,200-5,000 an ounce over the next 12-24 months, NDB Wealth Management said in an ANI-carried report, as central-bank buying and Asian investor demand increasingly set prices rather than US rates. It cites 289 tonnes of central-bank buying in Q2 2026 and record Asian gold-fund inflows of nearly 70 tonnes in H1; the $4,200-5,000 range is its 50%-probability base case.

items.title: World Gold Council: India's seasonal gold demand shows early strength
items.summary: Domestic discounts narrowed from an average of $66 an ounce in September to $8 as of October 16, the World Gold Council says, as seasonal demand gathered pace. September gold ETF inflows hit a seven-month high of Rs 44.5 billion (about 3 tonnes), with Rs 17.22 billion (1.2 tonnes) more in the first half of October. September imports fell to $1.8 billion, the lowest since March 2024.

items.title: Russia sells 62 tonnes of gold in biggest reserve drawdown since 1998
items.summary: Bank of Russia data show gold reserves fell another 200,000 troy ounces (6.2 tonnes) in September, to 72.8 million ounces (2,264 tonnes) — the lowest since end-2019. The central bank has cut holdings for ten straight months, disposing of about 62 tonnes since December 2025, as the Kremlin covers a widening budget deficit; the Finance Ministry expects the 2026 deficit to reach 7.3 trillion roubles.

items.title: Silver Surplus Calls May Overstate the Impact of Weaker Solar Demand
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and StoneX have shifted to surplus language - a possible physical silver surplus in 2027, or a 2026 surplus of about five weeks of demand (~107 Moz). Przemyslaw Radomski argues the solar decline is largely already counted: Metals Focus and the Silver Institute already assume PV demand falls 19% to 151 Moz inside a 46.3 Moz 2026 shortfall.

items.title: Gem, jewellery exporters heave a sigh of relief as the US puts off punitive tax
items.summary: Indian gem and jewellery exporters expect US orders to revive after President Trump waived proposed 100% punitive duties on goods from top Russian oil buyers. The US remains India's largest export market ahead of Christmas demand, and industry exports rose 13% to $14.30 billion in the fiscal first half. IBJA data showed domestic gold fell 5% in the past month to Rs 145,944 per 10 grams.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 profit more than doubles on higher metal prices; silver output up 20%
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc's consolidated net profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher metal prices and record output lifted revenue 76.5% to Rs 15,093 crore, margin widening to 42%. Silver production rose 20% to 173 tonnes and silver sales revenue more than doubled, driving about 45% of profitability; Jefferies said firmer silver prices improved the profit outlook.

items.title: India's festive and wedding season demand picks up as prices ease
items.summary: Jewellers report improving footfall as the festive and wedding season begins, with manufacturers seeing strong orders and buyers favouring lighter designs and old-gold exchange deals, which rose over 10%. Gold slipped about 5% in India in September, and listed jewellers posted 20-30% revenue growth in the July-September quarter.
